English translation from the Modern Amharic of the EOTC Bible (nehemiah-osc.org) by Claude (Anthropic) with collaborator, May 2026. Three books: 1 Mq 36 chapters (Maqabis-of-Benjamin martyrology vs Ṣiruṣaydan); 2 Mq 21 chapters (Maqabis-of-Moab conversion + sons' martyrdom + Ṣiruṣaydan's death); 3 Mq 10 chapters (homiletic + angelological dialogue + Satan-refused-Adam tradition + resurrection-doctrine).

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Second Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan II) (c. 600 AD)

OPENS Ch 15: RESURRECTION-DOCTRINE INTRODUCTION extending Ch 14's anti-sectarian polemic with a positive-systematic exposition. The chapter's framing: 'Now hear concerning the resurrection of the dead — how God shall raise them up.' The doctrinal-exposition genre parallels: 1 CORINTHIANS 15 (Pauline systematic-resurrection-treatise — the canonical-Christian model); WISDOM OF SOLOMON 3:1-9 + 5:15-23 (the righteous-immortality systematic-exposition); 4 MACCABEES 9-18 (the philosophical-soul-treatise embedded in the martyrdom-narrative); ENOCH 22 (the four-chambers-of-Sheol doctrine — γ.4.4 Mäṣḥafä Hēnok parallel). Meqabyan's distinctive feature: the resurrection-doctrine exposition is FRAMED AS REVELATION-TO-MAQABIS-OF-MOAB — the converted-Gentile-king receives the doctrinal-instruction directly. This pedagogical-framing makes Maqabis-of-Moab a DOCTRINAL-TYPE for the Gentile-convert who receives full-doctrinal-instruction within Israel's covenant-tradition.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Second Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan II) (c. 600 AD)

MATERIALIST-SADDUCEE REFUTATION (vv. 11-18): the Sadducean-denial-of-resurrection is refuted by appeal to GOD'S CREATIVE-POWER. The argumentation: if God could create the body from dust-and-nothing at first, He can re-create it from dust at resurrection — the standard-Christian-patristic CREATION-TO-RESURRECTION argument. Direct parallels: 2 MACCABEES 7:28 (the mother to her youngest son — 'I beseech thee, my son, look upon the heaven and the earth, and all that is therein, and consider that God made them of things that were not; and so was mankind made likewise' — the canonical-creatio-ex-nihilo resurrection-argument); ROMANS 4:17 ('God, who quickeneth the dead, and calleth those things which be not as though they were'); HEBREWS 11:19 ('accounting that God was able to raise him up, even from the dead' — Abraham's binding-of-Isaac interpreted); 1 CLEMENT 24-26 (the resurrection-argument-from-nature). The Meqabyan argument compresses the canonical-Hebrew-Bible + LXX-Maccabean + Pauline argumentation into one systematic exposition.
